title: Disks
unavailable: This server does not provide the disk list.
systemNote: This is the system disk: LordOS does not let you format, erase or unmount it from here.
adminNote: Only an administrator can change internal disks.
notMountedUsage: Not mounted: usage is shown once mounted.
unmounted: Unmounted. It can be removed now.
ejected: Ejected. It can be removed now.
label: Label
noSmart: This disk does not report its health (SMART): this happens with virtual disks, images and many cards.
healthHint.warning: There are signs of wear (reallocated or pending sectors, low spare): a backup is a good idea.
healthHint.failing: The disk says it will fail soon. Copy your data now and replace it.
healthHint.unknown: The disk answered, but without enough data.
prefailNote: * pre-fail: if its value drops below the threshold, the disk is about to fail.
confirm.disk: The WHOLE disk {disk} ({model}, {size}) will be erased:
confirm.empty: It has no partitions or recognizable data.
confirm.typeName: To confirm, type the disk name: {name}
fsHint.fat32: Works everywhere (Windows, macOS, Linux, TVs). Files up to 4 GB.
fsHint.exfat: For large USB sticks and external disks: Windows, macOS and Linux, without the 4 GB limit.
fsHint.ext4: The Linux one: permissions and links. Windows and macOS cannot read it without extra software.
fsHint.ntfs: The Windows one. Linux and macOS read it; macOS needs extra software to write.
badLabel: Invalid name: up to {n} characters, without / \ : * ? " < > |. In FAT32, only plain letters, digits, space, _ and -.
formatWholeHint: The whole disk gets an MBR table with a single partition.
noTools: There are no formatting programs (dosfstools, exfatprogs, e2fsprogs).
eraseHint.quick: Erases the partition table and signatures: data is no longer visible, but special tools could recover it.
eraseHint.zero: Writes zeros over the whole device. It takes a while (minutes or hours on a USB stick), but leaves nothing.
renameUnmount: Unmount it first to rename it.
imageHint: Choose an .iso or .img image (from your folder or your disks). It is copied as is and then verified by reading the disk back.
imageNone: No .iso or .img images found in your folder: type the path.
imageTooBig: The image ({size}) does not fit on the disk ({disk}).
